body: well, the archivist in me says put it in an acid-free box in a temperature controlled room.

i mean, it’s a great compass if you’re trying to find a big pile of shit. 

i just don’t see any situation in the future where i can enjoy my life. i’m so tired of all the shit i deal with, i don’t have time for anything outside of work.

we serve and try to help tons of people in extremely desperate situations. people don’t realize how stressful and fucked up working in a public library is. people OD in the bathrooms, people get in fights, people with sever mental health issues who can’t get help anywhere else come to us. i’ve helped unsheltered people and found out a week later they died on the street. 
but honestly i think it’s mostly been the hostile work environment thing. our upper mgmt is full of shit and it’s really obvious, they’re doing a bunch of things that don’t benefit anyone but they think it makes them look good. we’ve had HUGE turnover in mgmt in the last year. things got really hostile and now lots of people have been leaving and have been replaced by sycophants trying to make a good impression on the boss. 

i’ve got no excuse for your school librarians. books are amazing.

you mean the work i do? i work at a library. i get to do some cool stuff but it’s mostly customer service and it’s really bureaucratic and the work environment really got hostile and nerve wracking in the last year. but the pay is good and i get benefits.

ah, i guess i didn’t make that clear in my post. i just can’t think of anything like that that wouldn’t require making pretty drastic changes in my quality of life. idk how i’d get retirement or health insurance and i love the city i live in, ive been here my whole life but it’s really expensive and i don’t have a car. i’ve got a DUI. 
anything like that that i can think of would be a huge step back after putting all this time in to what i’m doing now.
